summary: Games Monitor gives 3, 834 jobs in 2018, 4, 560 in 2021 and 4, 291 in 2023. Most recent decline reflects companies moving outside the games definition. Includes self-employed specialists and applied games.

search_log.outcome: No dedicated complete games workforce series found; report links official employment and business sources.
Association archive and full report inspected.

sources.title: Games Monitor 2024
sources.publisher: Dutch Games Association / Dutch Game Garden / NEO Observatory
sources.notes: Primary-authored report publicly mirrored by InvestGame; survey conducted January/February 2025; employment observation 2023, despite report title 2024.

sources.title: Games Monitor 2015
sources.publisher: Dutch Game Garden / TNO / NEO Observatory
sources.notes: Primary-authored report mirrored by Boekman. May 2015 LISAdata; survey 130 companies; estimated remaining 35 companies with missing employment.

series.label: Dutch games-industry jobs including self-employed specialists
series.industry_scope: Development, production, publishing, facilitation and electronic distribution; entertainment and applied games; specialist services and freelancers; excludes retail and gambling
series.geography_note: See comparison note; local operations rather than nationality unless explicitly stated
series.worker_status: Employees and active self-employed specialists; founders with main employment elsewhere not active jobs
series.contractor_treatment: Specialist freelancers and one-person subcontractors included; no independent contractor share
series.method: LISA employment register, survey, company websites and LinkedIn cross-checks
series.comparison_note: Same published definition; most 2021–2023 decline is reclassification of company focus, not job loss. No 2019 observation.
series.term_translation: Dutch games-industry jobs including self-employed specialists
